review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it against the LoewnerFlow definitions (deficit_nonneg_iff, nonneg_until, stop_bounds). I looked for repeated non-trivial blocks. The strongest case is the "deficit stays nonneg up to the stopping time, hence all three constraints hold" step. It appears about nine times, in two argument styles: the generic (U, ρ, δ) form and the Cutoff/Brownian form. Other repeats are weaker, and I did not report them. These are the `.mono (Icc_subset_Icc ..)` restriction of position_derivWithin, which is short, and the `continuous_const.mul (hc.comp continuous_real_toNNReal)).continuousOn` term, which is trivial. The derivative computations in the Swallowing section are routine calculus and differ from each other. The finding is a modest-size deduplication. Part of its value is that the Brownian-form call repeats a long argument list (bounds, initial_deficit_brownian). I did not compile the proposed lemmas.

findings.problem: The same step is re-derived about nine times. Initial positivity of the deficit gives nonnegativity up to the stopping time (`nonneg_until`). `deficit_nonneg_iff` then turns that into the three constraints `ρ ≤ radius ∧ ε ≤ im ∧ δ ≤ sine`. The call is spelled out in full each time with eight or more arguments. Sites in the generic form are lines 55–56, 77–78, 103–104, 184–185, 198–199 and 217–218. Sites in the Cutoff form are lines 399–401, 577–579 and 584–586. The Cutoff form also repeats `C.initial_deficit_brownian κ B sample hz hu hc hb0` and `⟨(C.bounds κ B sample).1,le_rfl⟩` verbatim. Only the final projection (`.1`, `.2.1`, `.2.2`, or the whole triple) differs between sites. This clutters each proof with plumbing and makes any change to the exit-time API a nine-place edit.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two lemmas, each stated once with the proof being the existing composition.

(1) In LoewnerLocalized, next to `source_until_stop`:
`lemma constraints_until_stop (U : C(I, ℝ)) (z : ℂ) (ρ δ : ℝ) (h0 : 0 < deficit hε hT.le U z ρ δ 0) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc 0 (stop hε hT.le U z ρ δ)) : ρ ≤ radius hε hT.le U z t ∧ ε ≤ (position hε hT.le U z t).im ∧ δ ≤ sine hε hT.le U z t := (deficit_nonneg_iff hε hT.le U z ρ δ t).1 (nonneg_until hε hT.le hT U z ρ δ h0 ht)`.
The existing sites become `(constraints_until_stop hε hT U z ρ δ h0 ht).2.1` and so on. In `terminal_cases` and `clock_bounds_stop` the `τ` instance is `constraints_until_stop … ⟨hb.1, le_rfl⟩`.

(2) In `Cutoff`, using the section variables of the later block (`include h hz hu hc hb0` is not needed for this one, so only `hz hu hc hb0` are used):
`lemma stop_constraints : (2*z.im)*Real.exp (-u) ≤ radius C.height_pos C.horizon.coe_nonneg (C.paths κ B sample) z (C.stopTime κ B sample) ∧ C.height ≤ (position C.height_pos C.horizon.coe_nonneg (C.paths κ B sample) z (C.stopTime κ B sample)).im ∧ C.angle ≤ sine C.height_pos C.horizon.coe_nonneg (C.paths κ B sample) z (C.stopTime κ B sample) := constraints_until_stop C.height_pos C.horizon_pos _ z _ C.angle (C.initial_deficit_brownian κ B sample hz hu hc hb0) ⟨(C.bounds κ B sample).1, le_rfl⟩`.
Then rewrite:
- `value_bound`: `have hd := C.stop_constraints κ B sample hz hu hc hb0` (replaces lines 398–401; the final `simpa … using hd.1` is unchanged).
- `radius_lower`: `rw [← C.source_radius …]; exact (C.stop_constraints κ B sample hz hu hc hb0).1`.
- `value_eq_source`: `have hh := (C.stop_constraints κ B sample hz hu hc hb0).2.1`.
findings.benefit: Each affected proof shrinks to a one-line projection. The shared fact (the three exit constraints persist up to the stopping time) is named and stated once, and the long Brownian-specific argument list is no longer copied three times. Future changes to the `deficit` / `exitPath` API need one edit instead of about nine. Readers see which constraint each proof uses (`.1` radius, `.2.1` height, `.2.2` sine) instead of parsing a nested term.
